verdicts.label: supported
verdicts.evidence: the S1 N-terminal domain exhibits signals of positive selection in the pairwise comparisons in all four coronavirus genera

verdicts.label: contradicted
verdicts.evidence: many changes in the S protein have been under positive selection by altering the receptor-binding affinity, reducing antibody neutralization activities, or affecting T-cell responses
verdicts.reason: The statement says antibody neutralization was elevated, but the abstract says these changes reduced antibody neutralization activities.

verdicts.label: supported
verdicts.evidence: the S gene, particularly the S1 region, has experienced positive selection in both SARS-CoV-2 and other coronaviruses

verdicts.label: not_addressed
verdicts.evidence: coronaviruses from different genera being able to recognize the same receptor and coronaviruses from the same genus able to bind distinct receptors

verdicts.label: supported
verdicts.evidence: Adaptively introgressed variants were enriched for moderate-effect splicing variants, consistent with positive selection for alternative spliced alleles following introgression

verdicts.label: not_addressed
verdicts.evidence: We further identified potentially pathogenic splicing variants found only in Neanderthals and Denisovans in genes related to sperm maturation and immunity
verdicts.reason: The abstract reports pathogenic variants unique to these hominins but makes no claim that they caused extinction.

verdicts.label: supported
verdicts.evidence: Of the 5,169 alleles tested in this massively parallel splicing reporter assay (MaPSy), we report 962 exonic splicing mutations that correspond to differences in exon recognition between extant and extinct hominins

verdicts.label: contradicted
verdicts.evidence: splice-disrupting variants experienced greater purifying selection in anatomically modern humans than that in Neanderthals
verdicts.reason: The statement says smaller purifying selection in modern humans, but the abstract says greater.
